text: Designing a good REST API is about making life easier for developers. First, keep your endpoints clear and logical, like `/users` or `/orders`, rather than confusing actions. Always use proper HTTP status codes—`200` for success, `404` for missing resources, and `400` for bad requests—so clients understand what happened. Never skip documentation; a well-written guide with examples helps everyone use your API correctly. Finally, plan for versioning, such as `/v1/users`. This allows you to make changes and add features without breaking existing apps that depend on your service. A thoughtful API saves time, reduces errors, and builds trust with its users.
